title: diSCover – Digital Language Mediation in the Context of Trauma-Related Disorders and Therapy Needs Among Asylum Seekers and Their Families: A Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing Video-Based and In-Person Language Mediation
summary: The study aims to investigate which interpreting setting is most helpful in trauma-focused psychotherapy for asylum seekers and individuals with a migration background. A total of 126 adult patients will participate in the study. The allocation of the therapy setting, either in-person interpreting or video interpreting, will be randomly assigned. The study will examine whether there are differences in the acceptance of video and in-person interpreting in the treatment of trauma-related disorders among asylum seekers from the perspective of all participants. To this end, patients, psychotherapists, and interpreters will be surveyed using short questionnaires during three consecutive therapy sessions. Additionally, the study will investigate differences between the video and in-person interpreting settings in terms of the patients' sense of security, the influence of evaluative anxiety on the sense of security, and changes in symptom severity over time. To collect this data, self-report questionnaires will be completed before and after the three therapy sessions.

interventions.name: Video-based language mediation in trauma-focused psychotherapy (baseline assessment, 3 measurement points during therapy, final assessment)
In-person language mediation in trauma-focused psychotherapy (baseline assessment, 3 measurement points during therapy, final assessment)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Refugees and people with a migration background, treated in the trauma outpatient clinic of the PSO (Psychosocial Oncology) at the University Hospital Carl Gustav Carus Dresden, who require language mediation for treatment.
- Traumatic experience according to DSM-5 (APA, 2015).
- Capacity to consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute psychotic disorder
- Severe acute suicidality
